note: Style plate: every Gallic War picture uses this as its style reference.
style: A Roman history painting in the manner of Jean-Léon Gérôme and Lawrence Alma-Tadema: crisp academic realism, brilliant Mediterranean daylight, clear warm light and deep blue shadow, precise archaeological detail of 58 BC, rich painterly finish. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, lettering, signature, border or black bars.

beats.text: A Gaulish hill-fort (oppidum) of 58 BC above a wide river in brilliant afternoon light: timber-laced stone ramparts, thatched round houses, smoke rising; in the foreground a Roman cavalry patrol with red cloaks and Montefortino helmets halts on the riverbank while long-haired Gaulish warriors with moustaches, checked trousers, cloaks and torcs watch from the ford. Wide view, deep landscape, blue distance.

A Roman marching camp of 58 BC at golden evening light beside a broad river in Gaul: square earth rampart and palisade, rows of leather tents, the general's tent with red banners, legionaries in mail shirts cooking at fires, horses picketed, the eagle standard planted, forested hills and a pale gold sky. Wide view; figures small.
